clue.text: Actor that's given two boys a sort of swatter

parts.note: Pat and Rick are two boys' names, side by side

indicators.note: a sort of swatter is a version of that word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor is handed a fly-swatter of some kind by a couple of lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges SWATTER into the surname STEWART. Sir Patrick Stewart is the English actor of Star Trek fame, one of this puzzle's theme of Stewarts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Patrick Stewart is a well-known stage and screen performer, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Bananas on toast? Lets rip — they're a source of gas!

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, telling us to jumble the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Bananas on toast are blamed for flatulence: they make you let rip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' rearranges the fourteen letters of ON TOAST LETS RIP. Gas is the American word for petrol, which the British call petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling stations sell gasoline, the American name for motor fuel, so they are where drivers obtain it.

clue.text: Came true? No doubt — not even questionable

indicators.note: something questionable is doubtful or dodgy, signalling the letters gathered are rearranged
keeping only the odd-numbered letters of doubt, the not-even ones

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a prediction came true, and is told it did beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not even' keeps D, U, T, the odd letters of DOUBT; 'questionable' rearranges TRUE, NO and DUT. 'Came true?' looks like the definition but only 'Came' is.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out for something is to attend or show up, so the phrasal verb is a synonym of came.

clue.text: Start off season in team

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off, removing its first letter

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A footballer begins the season playing in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes W, the first letter of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Internazionale of Milan, an Italian football club, is commonly called by this short name, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: Most benevolent sort, in case where one is imprisoned

parts.note: a sort is a kind, a type

indicators.note: the one is shut inside the word for in case, like a prisoner in a cell

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A kindly sort of jailer, perhaps, sympathetic to the case of someone locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is imprisoned' puts I inside LEST to make LIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindliest is the superlative of kindly, so it describes the most warm-hearted and generous.

clue.text: See 1
Actor's back in cast? Just a small part

indicators.note: in places the actor's back letter inside the word for cast

parts.note: to cast off skin, as a snake does, is to shed it

indicators.note: the back of Actor is its final letter

explanation.surface: An actor complains they have been cast in a tiny role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' takes R, the last letter of Actor (the 's is just 'is'); 'in' places it inside SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny fragment or scrap, a little piece of something larger.

clue.text: Lament 10-0 thrashing, with feeling

indicators.note: a thrashing beats something up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the score written as letters: 10 looks like IO and 0 like O

explanation.surface: A fan mourns a ten-nil hammering, heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashing' rearranges LAMENT plus IOO, the score 10-0 read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional speech is full of feeling, so this adjective matches the adverbial phrase in sense.

clue.text: Shakespearean character ruining second part of King Lear

indicators.note: ruining the word wrecks it, so its letters are rearranged
the second letter of the word King

explanation.surface: Someone is spoiling the second half of King Lear in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second part of' takes I, the second letter of King, and 'ruining' rearranges it with LEAR. The surface wants Act 2 of the tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in The Tempest, a role from one of the Bard's plays.

clue.text: Our Father's earnest request that rain won't stop play?

definitions.meaning: Our Father is the opening and common name of the Christian ... taught by Jesus; the 's is 'is'

definitions.text: earnest request that rain won't stop play?
definitions.meaning: Lord's is the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A churchgoer prays that the cricket will not be rained off.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer beginning Our Father is called after the Lord who taught it; read again, Lord's is the cricket ground.

clue.text: Sailor heads for original top deck

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the heads of the words that follow are their first letters

explanation.surface: A sailor makes for the top deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' takes O and T, the first letters of original and top. 'deck' looks nautical but is a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards come as a pack used for fortune-telling, so the name is an example of a pack of cards.

clue.text: Give eg morphine to Scot? Er … Ian, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as one possible arrangement among many, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Should we sedate the Scotsman? Er... Ian, maybe, since Ian is a typical Scottish name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SCOT, ER and IAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: To drug someone with an opiate such as morphine puts them into a stupor, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: A little cricket game Liberal journalist decided against

parts.note: an over is a short unit of play in cricket, six balls
RU is rugby union
ED is an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A Liberal journalist writes about a short cricket game and rules it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Overruling is rejecting a decision or objection, as a judge does, so it means ruling against it.

clue.text: Returning soldier meets John in the White House

indicators.note: returning sends the soldier's letters back the other way

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
john is slang for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home meets a President named John in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns GI into IG. 'the White House' calls up the President's residence, but the house is white because it is snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow shelter is a dome built of white blocks, a playful description of it as a home.

clue.text: Twin street with A-road? As a rule, that's unfair

parts.note: a double is a twin, a lookalike
and means with, as in fish and chips
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road; an A-road is a British main road

explanation.surface: A town planner wonders whether to pair a street with a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule applied differently to different people is unfair, which is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Welsh lake reportedly similar to a musical instrument

parts.note: Bala Lake, Llyn Tegid, is the largest natural lake in Wales

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are spoken and spelt as they sound

parts.note: similar to a means like a

explanation.surface: A Welsh lake is said to look like an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: BALA is a town and lake in North Wales. 'reportedly' turns 'like a' into LAIKA, spelt by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a triangular, three-stringed Russian instrument of the lute family.

clue.text: Laughter as wife leaves tweet (gin drunk)

indicators.note: the wife leaves, so her letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a twitter is a bird's tweeting chirp

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A wife walks out as someone posts a tipsy tweet with gin in hand, to general amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes W out of TWITTER to make TITTER; 'drunk' rearranges GIN as ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittering is nervous, half-suppressed giggling, a kind of laughing.

clue.text: Toughening up of Queen before beheading somewhere in London

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain, 1702-14

indicators.note: beheading takes off the head, the first letter

parts.note: Ealing is a district of west London

explanation.surface: A queen being toughened up before her execution in a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a west London district; 'beheading' loses its first letter, and 'before' just sets the queen in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing is heating then slowly cooling metal or glass to make it less brittle, so it strengthens the material.

clue.text: See 1
Gossiping with model five times, interrupting Gail getting off with Neil

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

indicators.note: the Ts break into the pair of names at several points, so all go into one mix
getting off together suggests the letters are thoroughly mixed up, so the whole lot is rearranged

parts.note: T abbreviates time, so five times is five Ts

explanation.surface: Gossip about Gail getting together with Neil, involving a model on five occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The names, rearranged as ILEALING, have six Ts spread through them rather than in one block, so the parse treats them as one pool. 'times' gives T because T abbreviates time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter about other people, so engaging in it is gossiping.

clue.text: See 8
Fish not cooked in right oil, ultimately

indicators.note: in puts the uncooked word between the two final letters
ultimately points to the last letters of right and oil

parts.note: raw food has not been cooked

explanation.surface: Raw fish served in the right oil, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T and L, the last letters of right and oil; 'in' puts RAW between them. 'Fish' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to fish by dragging a net through the water, so it is a specific kind of the verb.

clue.text: Topless rural walk, a leisurely one

indicators.note: topless means the top letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a ramble is a walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: A topless stroll in the country, taken at an easy pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes the R from RAMBLE. 'one' in the definition stands for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is a slow, relaxed stroll, so it is a walk taken at an easy pace.

clue.text: Sort of TV channel broadcast after 10, including return of ER

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered
including means taking in, so the reversed pair goes inside the anagram

parts.note: 10 written as letters looks like IO

indicators.note: the return of the letters means they are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A channel that goes on air after ten o'clock, showing repeats of the hospital drama ER.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns ER round, and 'including' sets it after the F of the anagram; ten is written as the letters IO. ER here is the TV series, not the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel that viewers can watch without subscription is described this way, so it names a type of television service.

clue.text: Binge beginning in French Quarter

indicators.note: the beginning of French is its first letter

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A drinking spree starting in the French Quarter of New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning in' takes F from French. 'French Quarter' reads as the New Orleans district, but Quarter is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large, lavish meal, an occasion of overindulgence like a binge.

clue.text: Friendly country dance, after exchanging two letters

indicators.note: two letters of the dance change places, rearranging it

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A sociable nation's dance, after a couple of letters swap places.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and O of TANGO swap places. 'Friendly' is not a mere adjective: Cook named Tonga the Friendly Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga, the Pacific kingdom, is known as the Friendly Islands, so it is that friendly nation.

clue.text: Essential passages from old books Gail ordered, about sex

parts.note: B abbreviates book, so books is two Bs

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of Gail are rearranged
about turns the word round, reading it backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Steamy extracts from old books, rearranged by Gail around a sexual theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges GAIL as LIGA; 'about' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Obbligato parts are instrumental lines a score marks as indispensable, so in music they are passages that must be played.

clue.text: Curious about one getting rowdy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the curious word goes round the one

parts.note: a nosy person is curious, inquisitive
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person turns unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NOSY around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy people are loud and disorderly, which is close to the sense of making a lot of din.

clue.text: More curious about women getting seduced by potentially great actor

indicators.note: about means going round, so the curious word encloses the rest

parts.note: stranger means more odd, more curious

indicators.note: the women are taken in by the anagram, so W goes inside it
potentially great is what great could become, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd tale of women seduced by an actor who might become great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges the five letters of great to EARTG; 'getting seduced by' takes W inside that; 'about' wraps the curious word round the result, splitting it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart Granger was a British film star of the 1940s and 50s, so he is an example of a performer.
